llm.summary: The skill largely does what its description promises (deploy a Portal and run a local bridge), but it asks for high‑privilege things (SSH private key, local OpenClaw hooks token, writes systemd/nginx, and requests relaxing OpenClaw exec security) and the registry metadata is inconsistent with the SKILL.md — proceed only after careful review and limiting privileges.

dimensions.detail: The code and instructions match the stated purpose: deploying a Portal on a VPS and running a local Bridge that uses an API key and hooks token. However the registry metadata (required env vars: none) contradicts SKILL.md/CONFIG.md which list AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL and OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and required binaries (python3, ssh). That metadata mismatch is an integrity problem that should be resolved before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and included scripts read and write local config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, ~/.openclaw/agent-p2p-admin.txt), request the OpenClaw hooks token, ask the user for an SSH private key, and instruct the agent to execute install scripts that modify system services (systemd, Nginx) and run certbot. The skill also posts to the OpenClaw hooks endpoint to 'wake' the main session — these actions access and transmit sensitive local state and could be abused if credentials are mishandled.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal registry install spec, but many install scripts (auto_install.py, install.sh, scripts/deploy_portal.py) are included and will run shell commands, clone a GitHub repo, apt/pip install packages, configure nginx, certbot, and create systemd services both locally and remotely via SSH. Executing those scripts gives the skill broad system-level effects; while the GitHub source is referenced, automatic remote execution and requests to relax agent exec security increase risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested secrets (API key, Hub URL, OpenClaw gateway URL, hooks token, and an SSH private key for VPS deployment) are relevant to deploying and operating the Portal but are high‑privilege. The skill additionally auto-reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to obtain the hooks token (not just relying on declared env vars). It also stores generated admin credentials and writes gateway.env locally. Reading/writing these local files and requesting an SSH private key is proportional to deployment needs but materially increases attack surface and requires careful user controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always: true, but its install metadata requests that OpenClaw relax exec policy (exec_security: full, exec_ask: off) so the skill can run complex shell operations without prompts. That change is a platform‑level privilege escalation and substantially increases risk if granted. The skill also installs a long‑running bridge (systemd service) and writes persistent config/local files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will deploy code on a remote VPS and modify your local system and OpenClaw configuration. Before installing: 1) Resolve the metadata inconsistency: confirm which env vars and permissions the skill actually needs. 2) Never hand over your primary SSH private key or OWNER_KEY — create a dedicated limited SSH key and limited API key for this skill. 3) Do not relax OpenClaw exec security globally; prefer interactive/manual execution of installation steps or run the installer in a controlled environment (container or disposable VM). 4) Audit the included scripts (auto_install.py, install.sh, scripts/deploy_portal.py, vps/main.py) yourself or with a trusted admin before running; these scripts run shell commands as root on a VPS and write systemd/nginx configs. 5) Note that some client code disables SSL verification and skips certificate checks — consider fixing verify=False / CERT_NONE before production use. 6) If you proceed, limit network exposure (firewall, VPS user permissions), rotate tokens/keys after setup, and consider running the Portal on a dedicated account/VM you control. If you want, I can list the exact lines that read local secrets, perform SSH/deploy actions, or prepare a minimal checklist to safely perform manual install steps.
